newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TENNIS-SOUTH AFRICA BEAT RUSSIA IN DAVIS CUP FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SOUTH AFRICA BEAT RUSSIA IN DAVIS CUP FIRST ROUND.

text.p: South Africa reached the second round of the Davis Cup world group when their doubles pair Ellis Ferreira and Grant Stafford clinched victory over Russia on Sunday.
Ferreira and Stafford beat Andrei Olhovsky and Andrei Cherkasov 6-2 3-6 6-0 6-2 in a match postponed from Saturday to give South Africa a winning 3-0 lead.

Andrei Chesnokov salvaged a measure of pride for Russia when he upset world number eight Wayne Ferreira later on Sunday but the second of the dead reverse singles, between Cherkasov and Marcos Ondruska,was abandoned, in accordance with Davis Cup rules, as the Russian had played more than 30 games earlier in the day.
The decision left the result at 3-1 and South Africa facing either former champions Sweden or Switzerland in the second round in April.
"It's a great feeling to have won this tie. We were expected to win but the first three matches were all tough. This victory is very satisfying," South African captain Danie Visser said.

On-court temperatures reached 42 degrees Celsius as the South African doubles pair swept through the first set 6-2 in only half an hour, with the left-handed Ferreira winning several points on crunching forehand drives.
The Russians fought back with three breaks of serve to take the second set 6-3 as Olhovsky, ranked 23rd in world doubles, began to mix powerful groundstrokes with some intelligently-placed lobs.
"They threw up a lot of lobs in that set and, for quite a while, the sun was right in our faces in the middle of the court," Ferreira said. "But once the sun moved it wasn't that bad."
Despite intense humidity, the South Africans breezed through the next two sets in only 45 minutes for the loss of just two games.
The 31-year-old Chesnokov broke a lacklustre Wayne Ferreira twice in the deciding third set to win their reverse singles rubber 6-2 6-7 6-2 in one hour 47 minutes.
Wayne Ferreira -- who is not related to Ellis -- had beaten Cherkasov in a five-set match which finished on Saturday after being interrupted by rain on Friday.
In Friday's opening singles, Ondruska beat Russian number one Chesnokov 7-6 6-3 3-6 4-6 7-5 after nearly four hours on court.
